name: Liujiang Zhuang
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Chen, Honglei & Chalernsak Pikulsri. 2025. Prosodic structure and rhythmic patterns in Zhuang folk songs: a metrical phonological perspective. Forum for Linguistic Studies 7(12). doi:10.30564/fls.v7i12.11954
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Reports corpus percentages of 'prosodic word stress'-to-beat alignment in sung Zhuang (N/S/C dialect regions, none identified as Liujiang) but never states where word stress falls; not usable as a description.

sources.citation: Chen, Honglei et al. 2025. The development and characteristics of Zhuang folk songs in the Liujiang vernacular area, Guangxi, China. International Journal of Sociologies and Anthropologies Science Reviews. doi:10.60027/ijsasr.2025.6952
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Musicological; only says melodies follow 'the tonal characteristics of the Liujiang dialect'. No linguistic stress statement; not a language description.

sources.citation: Castro, Andy & Bruce Hansen. 2010. Hongshui He Zhuang dialect intelligibility survey. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2010-025. Dallas: SIL International. 110 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent on stress (a full-text search for stress/accent/unstressed: 0 hits). Liujiang Zhuang appears only as the neighbouring dialect area (north Laibin, Liucheng and western Luzhai varieties are said to belong to the Liujiang dialect); wordlists and RTT data are for Hongshui He points.

sources.citation: Edmondson, Jerold A. 1994. Change and variation in Zhuang. In K. L. Adams & T. J. Hudak (eds.), Papers from the Second Annual Meeting of the Southeast Asian Linguistics Society, 147-185. Tempe: Arizona State University Program for Southeast Asian Studies.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent. Comparative study of segmental and tonal sound changes across Zhuang survey points drawn from Zhuangyu Yinxi (1959); Liujiang is point 13 (also Yishan 15, Liucheng 16, Xincheng 17, Laibin N 14) in the cluster/preglottalized-stop/tone tables; no stress statement anywhere.

sources.citation: Edmondson, Jerold A. 1992. Some Kadai languages of northern Guangxi, China. In: The Third International Symposium on Language and Linguistics, 28-43. Bangkok: Chulalongkorn University.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent. pp. 35-37 treat Sanfang Zhuang, 'a lesser-studied kind of Zhuang, assigned to the Liujiang vernacular type': six tone values (51, 3231, 43, 21, 442, 313) with F0 plots, initials gw-/gj-/gjw-, comparison with Qiaoshan (Huanjiang). No word on stress or accent (scanned a full-text search for stress/accent/iamb/promin).

sources.citation: Luo Yongxian. 2008. Zhuang. In Diller, Edmondson & Luo (eds.), The Tai-Kadai Languages, 317-377. London: Routledge.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; library e-access not checked
sources.note: Modern English-language overview of Zhuang phonology (Northern Zhuang based); if it contains a sentence on stress in di/polysyllables it would be the citable English statement, though pan-Zhuang rather than Liujiang-specific.

sources.citation: Chen Xueni 陈雪妮. 2015. 壮语柳江话构词法分析. 温州职业技术学院学报 2015(3): 80-82; and Li Jinyang 李金阳 2023. 壮语南北方言状貌词比较研究——以柳江壮语与大新壮语为例. 玉林师范学院学报 2023(6): 43-54.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Recent first-hand Liujiang Zhuang papers on prefixes/post-attached syllables and ideophones; may note prosodic weakness of 词头, a proxy for stress placement.

sources.citation: He Shuang 何霜. 2007. 忻城壮语语气词研究 [Studies on discourse particles in Xincheng Zhuang]. PhD dissertation, 中央民族大学 Minzu University of China. (Glottolog 470231)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only Glottolog-listed description for liuj1238; Minzu University dissertations open with a 音系 overview of the fieldwork point (Xincheng, inside the Liujiang dialect area) which may state tone inventory and any stress/轻声 facts, and sentence particles are exactly where 轻读 remarks appear.

sources.citation: Zhang Junru 张均如 et al. 1999. 壮语方言研究 [A study of Zhuang dialects]. Chengdu: Sichuan Minzu Chubanshe. (36-point survey; 柳江百朋 is the Liujiang point, with 宜山, 柳城, 来宾 nearby)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The authoritative phonological description of the Liujiang survey point (声母/韵母/声调 chapters plus a general phonology chapter); the place most likely to carry any remark on 轻重音, weak prefix syllables (词头) or the absence of contrastive stress.

sources.citation: Qin Guosheng 覃国生. 1981. 壮语柳江话动词、形容词的后附成分. 民族语文 1981(4): 51-56.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: First-hand Liujiang Zhuang paper by a native-speaker linguist on post-verbal attached syllables; likely to say whether these syllables are read light/unstressed relative to the root, the closest thing to a stress statement in this literature.

sources.citation: 广西壮族自治区少数民族语言文字工作委员会研究室. 1959. 壮语音系 Zhuangyu Yinxi [Zhuang phonology] (internal fieldwork report, phonological systems of 56 Zhuang localities; source of Edmondson 1994's Liujiang/Yishan/Liucheng/Xincheng data).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Primary survey record for the Liujiang-area points; superseded by Zhang et al. 1999 but independently lists each locality's system.

sources.citation: Chen Xueni 陈雪妮. 2015. 壮语柳江话构词法分析 [Word formation in Liujiang Zhuang]. 温州职业技术学院学报 2015(3): 80-82.
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.access_detail: only an abstract or snippet reachable
sources.note: Abstract only: compounding, prefixes (词头) and post-attached syllables of Liujiang Zhuang; nothing on stress in the abstract.

sources.citation: He Shuang 何霜. 2007. 忻城壮语语气词研究 Xincheng Zhuangyu yuqi ci yanjiu [Studies on discourse particles in Xincheng Zhuang]. PhD dissertation, Minzu University of China (中央民族大学). (Glottolog ref 470231; the only descriptive reference Glottolog lists for liuj1238.)
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: Not seen; Chinese PhD theses of this type normally open with a phonology overview (声韵调) of the fieldwork point; whether it mentions 轻重音 is unknown. Related journal papers by He Shuang (2007, 2008, 2018, 2020 on 忻城壮语 grammaticalization) seen as NCPSSD abstracts only, all grammatical.

sources.citation: Qin Guosheng 覃国生. 1981. 壮语柳江话动词、形容词的后附成分 [Post-attached elements of verbs and adjectives in Liujiang Zhuang]. 民族语文 Minzu Yuwen 1981(4): 51-56.
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.access_detail: only an abstract or snippet reachable
sources.note: NCPSSD record + opening lines only (full text behind NCPSSD login): describes the single- and multi-syllable post-attached elements of Liujiang Zhuang verbs/adjectives; whether it comments on their prosodic weight (轻读) could not be checked.

sources.citation: Zhang Junru 张均如, Liang Min 梁敏, Ouyang Jueya 欧阳觉亚, Zheng Yiqing 郑贻青, Li Xulian 李旭练, Xie Jianyou 谢建猷. 1999. 壮语方言研究 Zhuangyu fangyan yanjiu [A study of Zhuang dialects]. Chengdu: 四川民族出版社.
sources.note: Not seen. The standard dialectological reference: phonological systems of 36 points including 柳江(百朋), 宜山(洛东), 柳城, 来宾, 忻城? etc; print only, no online copy reachable by automated download.
